title: Sunday · Cedar, v · the blade moon
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: The fifth of twelve. Night at the mill. The moon over the stack is a sawblade — the great circular blade from the floor, risen. Its teeth in the clouds. Played straight. The stack a full tree now.

panels.composition: Tier 1: the mill at night. The stack, a tall cedar now from its top, and over it, where the moon should be, a circular sawblade, silver, its teeth catching cloud.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, a ruined mill at night with a tall cedar growing from the top of its brick smokestack and above it in place of the moon a great circular sawblade silver against clouds, played straight, no words

panels.name: Blade moon

panels.composition: Tier 2: the blade's edge, close, the teeth, and the moonlight coming off them the way it comes off water.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, close-up of a circular sawblade's teeth against night cloud with silver light coming off them like moonlight on water, no words

panels.name: Teeth

panels.composition: Tier 3: the yard in bladelight. The shadow of the stack-tree. And on the ground, the blade's real self: the rusted saw on the floor where it always was. Held.
props: the real blade on the ground

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rust, a mill yard lit silver from above with the long shadow of a tree-topped smokestack and on the ground a rusted circular sawblade lying where it always was, no words
image.notes: Both blades: the moon and the rusted one on the ground. The sequence's honesty.

panels.name: The real one
